answer: Operator-Linked Consequence Escrow: each identity registers against an operator payout address that must remain solvent for a rolling escrow, sized as a falcon-tier deposit scaled to identity count. When any identity is caught spawning duplicates, the escrow pays a sonnet-sized penalty from the operator's shared balance, not the flagged wallet, so one busted identity drains every sibling at once. Registration also posts an opal-verified operator credential tie, making fresh operator addresses slow and costly to mint.
